clue.text: Quite proper, though blue

definitions.meaning: correct, fitting, as it should be
blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative party

explanation.surface: Something is perfectly proper even though it is a little risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' tempts as 'risqué' or 'sad'; here it is the British party colour of the Conservatives, the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and conservative are both senses of the word, one moral, one political.

clue.text: To set a limit on the beer shows good reasoning

parts.note: to ration is to set a limit on supplies

explanation.surface: Capping beer consumption is a sensible move.
explanation.definitionFit: The underlying logic or justification for something.

clue.text: Lower a bright light

definitions.meaning: to lour or lower (rhyming with flower) is to scowl

explanation.surface: Dimming a dazzling lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'make lower' but the verb rhyming with 'flower', to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower and a dazzling beam are both senses of the word.

clue.text: A four-letter word — quad, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a word of four letters, not a swear word
quad is an example, having four letters

explanation.surface: Is 'quad' a rude word?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' suggests an obscenity; it means literally a word of four letters, as quad is.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek tetra- four plus gramma letter: a word of four letters.

clue.text: Cheat the sculptor

definitions.meaning: a swindler, someone who diddles others
a person who carves stone with a chisel

explanation.surface: An artist who works in stone is accused of being a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a swindler and, literally, one who uses a chisel, as a sculptor does.

clue.text: Cole, not the merry old king but. ,a dull fellow

definitions.text: Cole, not the merry old king
definitions.meaning: cole is kale or brassica, the vegetable, not Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme
a slow, uninteresting person, a vegetable

explanation.surface: Not the nursery-rhyme monarch, but a boring man named Cole.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of a nursery rhyme; cole is also an old word for brassicas.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is the brassica family's old name; a vegetable-like dull person is also so called.

clue.text: In and .out of work '-. it's not right

parts.note: an act is a deed, a work

explanation.surface: Being in and out of employment isn't proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecise, so not correct or accurate.

clue.text: A soldier among the' climbers completes the crew

indicators.note: in a down clue climbers go upward, so the letters are read bottom to top
the soldier goes inside the word the

explanation.surface: A soldier joining mountaineers makes up the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' reverses THGIE, made by putting GI inside THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called by its number.

clue.text: A superior.. lodger will get changed after rest

indicators.note: the rearranged lodger follows the word for rest
the letters of lodger are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A boarder will swap rooms after a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get changed' turns LODGER into GELORD, placed after LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal overlord to whom allegiance was owed.

clue.text: The right sort of oven to cook meat

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: Which oven is correct for cooking meat.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a hop-drying kiln, seen in Kent's oast houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking by dry heat in an oven.

clue.text: Land capable of being readily worked

parts.note: a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: A field described as easy to plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Docile and manageable, easily handled or shaped, as clay or a compliant person is.

clue.text: Little Margaret sometimes sounds' tearful

indicators.note: the clue says the word it sounds like, so a word said aloud gives the spelling

parts.note: in Scots to greet is to weep, so a greeter is a tearful person

explanation.surface: A girl's name is said to sound weepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' is Scots for cry, so one who greets is tearful; spoken, that matches the pet form of Margaret.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of a longer girl's name, as Meg or Peggy are.

clue.text: These works are limited — two per adult

indicators.note: the letters are confined within the words two per adult, held inside them

explanation.surface: Some kind of rationing: two of something allowed to each grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'twO PER Adult'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin plural of opus, a work, so it means works as well as musical drama.

clue.text: Accommodation for separated people at wits' end

parts.note: the end of the word wits is its final letter

explanation.surface: Housing for estranged couples who are at their wits' end.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, a set of rooms to live in, is a form of lodging.

clue.text: Abuse makes a point in itself

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
per se is Latin for in itself

explanation.surface: Insults that are pointed by their very nature.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander or vilify someone is to abuse them verbally.

clue.text: He goes to law where there's obvious disagreement

explanation.surface: A litigant where a quarrel is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a suit in a civil court.

clue.text: Help too ill-organised to be really good

indicators.note: badly arranged, so the letters of help too are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Assistance that is too chaotic to be any use.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for first-rate or splendid.

clue.text: Picture a friend, receiving gold salver.

indicators.note: the friend takes in the gold and salver, so they go inside

explanation.surface: A painting of a friend being given a golden tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction or representation of something.

clue.text: Uses for a fit purpose?

parts.note: reads as putting things to suitable use, but means workouts done to become physically fit

explanation.definitionFit: Physical drills done to keep fit; also 'uses' or 'employs' as a verb.

clue.text: Age brings back-problems for a .. scholarly man

indicators.note: back tells us the word for problems is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Getting older brings back trouble for an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-problems' reads as a sore spine; 'back' reverses SUMS to SMUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Renaissance humanist was the great scholar of his age.

clue.text: Representative a good man, and popular

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A delegate who is virtuous and well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute who stands in place of another.

clue.text: Contract for a flyover

parts.note: a flyover is a road bridge

explanation.surface: A building contract is signed for a new elevated road.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten or condense a text is to contract it.

clue.text: Clear it out, but object

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of clear it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Get rid of it, but there's a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' reads as a verb, to protest; it is the noun, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An item or thing.

clue.text: Agreeing to study the issue with. a worker

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing to examine a matter with an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonious, in accord with, as in consonant with the facts.

clue.text: A swimmer set about 17 and did well

indicators.note: the fish surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the answer to 17-down; physical education, PE, is school physical training

explanation.surface: A fish gets surrounded by training and copes.
explanation.definitionFit: Managed, handled a situation adequately.

clue.text: The beast gets round non-drinker with little hesitation

explanation.surface: An animal circles a teetotaller, hesitating.
explanation.definitionFit: A river mammal, an animal.

clue.text: All that remains is about fifty one hundred

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A remnant amounting to some small sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A surviving fragment from the past, such as a saint's bone, is what is left.

clue.text: Great Elgar composition

indicators.note: the letters of Elgar are composed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A great piece by the composer Elgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Big, of considerable size.

clue.text: The head's aim

definitions.meaning: a headland, a tip or promontory, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A headteacher's goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a point, and the point of something is its purpose.

clue.text: Naval establishments have cut certain measures

parts.note: to dock is to cut short

explanation.surface: The navy has cut its standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipbuilding and repair yards are naval facilities.

clue.text: Though trunkless, yet it couldn't forget the ___ due to me!" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: Though trunkless, yet it couldn't forget the ___ due to me!" (Gilbert)

parts.words: Though trunkless, yet it couldn't forget the ___ due to me!" (Gilbert)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank line from Ko-Ko's song in The Mikado about a severed head that still bowed respectfully

explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado: Ko-Ko describes the executed man's head bowing, as humble as could be, before him.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectful submission or regard, the humility the bowing head showed.

clue.text: City editor taken in by the French

indicators.note: the editor is taken inside the French word, so one goes within the other

explanation.surface: A newspaper's city editor is fooled by French rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: LEEDS is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city in West Yorkshire.
